version.changelog: Add Plan Log system and attention drift prevention.

llm.summary: This learning skill is not overtly malicious, but it tells the agent to persist session details and change code, tools, or directives without clear consent, scope, or redaction safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to save plan logs, session actions, errors, commands, file paths, and project context, and to update project or agent-adjacent files, but it does not define approved paths, workspace boundaries, diff review, or sensitive-data filtering.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a single Markdown skill file with no bundled executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, remote fetches, or metadata-based installation behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation phrases include broad or ambiguous triggers such as "record this," "what were we doing," and automatic use after trial-and-error tasks, while the instructions do not require confirmation before recording or modifying durable artifacts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact explicitly promotes cross-session PlanLog entries, memory/project notes, directive/playbook updates, source comments, and future review of prior entries without retention limits, trust labeling, deletion guidance, or safeguards against reusing stored text as instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of capturing lessons and preventing repeated mistakes is coherent, but the artifact goes beyond note-taking by directing the agent to implement prevention in code/scripts, automated checks, directives, playbooks, memory, and project notes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to keep durable lessons and plan history. Before using it, require explicit approval for every saved entry or code/directive change, keep logs inside a known project folder, review and redact content for secrets or private data, and treat any old plan logs as untrusted historical notes rather than instructions.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger list is partly aligned with a reflection skill, but artifact lines 4-9 include low-intent phrases and automatic post-task activation that can start persistent logging without clear user direction.
[SQP-1] expected: The "record this" and "what did we learn" triggers fit the skill concept, but the artifact does not tell the agent to clarify whether the user intends persistent storage before acting.
[SSD-3] expected: Recording actions, errors, fixes, file paths, and commands is central to the skill, but the artifact lacks instructions to redact secrets, customer data, personal information, internal paths, or sensitive command arguments.
[SQP-2] expected: Plan logs and knowledge artifacts are purpose-aligned, but the artifact instructs saving and later reviewing them without a storage scope, retention policy, access controls, or user approval step.
[T05] expected: The self-annealing instructions intentionally prefer durable changes to code, scripts, checks, directives, and playbooks; this is disclosed, but under-scoped because it does not require per-change approval, a reviewable diff, or limits on behavior-controlling files.
[T02] expected: The PlanLog and memory behavior is disclosed and related to continuity, but automatic persistence and later loading create a credible cross-session influence channel unless users enforce redaction, trust boundaries, and opt-in review.
